issues: Stray pixel 'spray' scattered above the dorsal fin and around the body muddies the silhouette, reading as noise/particles rather than a solid lit phosphor creature.
Dolphin lacks the subtle rim-light edge from the reference; the interior is a uniform dither with hard blocky pixel steps, hurting organic quality.
A bright full-width segmented bar along the very bottom plus right-side metadata text (128BPM / PHR / MIN) is not in the spec and competes with the dolphin, giving a modern-visualizer feel.
The left tail fluke looks fragmented and partly disconnected from the body, weakening the silhouette read.
The water band contains a fairly bright straight horizontal line that pushes wave contrast above the 'subtle, low-contrast' target.
The FFT reads as a random scatter of dots rather than a clean, low, graded bar graph.
suggestions: Clean the dolphin silhouette: delete the stray spray pixels, join the tail fluke smoothly to the body, and add a 1px brighter rim-light outline so it reads as one solid lit object.
Cut bottom clutter: remove or strongly dim the full-width segmented bar and the right-side metadata text so the FFT stays a short low-contrast graph and the dolphin clearly dominates.
Lower wave-line brightness (especially the straight horizontal line) and constrain waves to two thin low-contrast rows within 15% of display height.
Give the dolphin organic volume with a gentle vertical dither gradient (brighter back edge / belly shading) instead of a flat uniform fill.
Tighten the glow: keep crisp pixel edges with a 1-2px halo and ensure bloom does not bleed the body or spray into fog.
Render the FFT as discrete vertical bars of graded height at low brightness rather than scattered dots, matching a real OEL spectrum readout.
